title: The Godsaeng Challenge
description:
The SNS feed is all about 'godsaeng' — the god-tier life.

5 AM wake-ups, miracle mornings, dawn workouts, English study, 30 minutes of reading.
Hashtags #godsaeng #miraclemorning #selfimprovement flood the timeline.

The people in the proof shots all look radiant.
{name} was watching that feed at 1 AM.

Envious, and strangely anxious.
Should I be living like that too.

choices.text: Start the godsaeng tomorrow. Alarm set for 5 AM.
choices.result_text:
He set the alarm for 5 AM.

Day one went fine. Day two too. From day three it crumbled.

But hey, three days was something.
Godsaeng is a test every single day. {name} just set the alarm again.

Maybe even the radiant ones were secretly repeating these same three days, over and over.

choices.text: Forget other people's godsaeng — live at my own pace
choices.result_text:
{name} put the phone down.

Whether others get up at 5 AM or not, his life runs on his own schedule.
Godsaeng, too, is just another pressure when measured against others.

Thinking that, his mind eased.
{name} was moving at his own speed — but still, one step at a time.

choices.text: Make a godsaeng proof account. Showing off might motivate me.
choices.result_text:
He made a godsaeng account on Instagram.

Dawn workout proof, book covers, today's resolutions.
Followers grew bit by bit. Likes came in.

But at some point, he got confused — was he getting up to work out, or to take the proof shot.

The distance between the shown life and the lived life — kept growing.

title: The Godsaeng Paradox
description:
Two months into the godsaeng life.

Dawn wake-ups, workouts, study, reading, side projects.
The to-do list was perfect. Keeping all of it, 24 hours wasn't enough.

Then one day {name} realized, blankly:

Even his rest time was spent watching 'self-improvement content.'
Playing felt guilty. Sitting still felt like falling behind.

Trying to live the god-life, his whole life became an assignment.

choices.text: Do nothing for a whole day. Real rest.
choices.result_text:
One Sunday, {name} did nothing.

Alarm off, to-do list unopened, just lying down.
At first it was anxious. The time felt wasted.

But by afternoon, his head was strangely clear.

Resting was part of the god-life too. He learned that after two months.
He'd hit the brakes right before burnout.

choices.text: Just grind more efficiently. Optimize the system.
choices.result_text:
{name} packed the schedule tighter.

Audiobooks during commutes, lectures during meals, reviews before bed.
Filled every gap. Efficiency rose.

But his body started sending signals.
Eye twitches, indigestion, waking at dawn.

Godsaeng and burnout were one sheet of paper apart.
{name} was walking that razor's edge.

title: The Broke Room
description:
A friend sent a KakaoTalk open chat link.

'The Broke Room.' 100 anonymous people gathered to police each other's spending.

Someone posts 'Spent 4,500 won at Starbucks' and
'Hey, that's 90 cups of instant coffee at home!' floods the comments.

Funny, but — strangely helpful.
{name} posted his spending for the day too.

'Convenience store lunchbox, 4,800 won.'

Three seconds later, the notifications started.

choices.text: Settle into the Broke Room. Get policed daily.
choices.result_text:
'Buy rice with that lunchbox money and cook at home!'
'4,800 won is six packs of ramyeon, get it together!'

Laughing turned into genuine reflection.

From that day, {name} pictured the Broke Room before buying anything.
The nagging of 100 anonymous people auto-played in his head.

Strangely, his monthly spending dropped.
He never knew shame could turn into money.

choices.text: Laugh once and leave. Don't want stress from this.
choices.result_text:
{name} read a few posts, burst out laughing, and quietly left.

Saving is good, but he didn't want to live feeling guilty over one 4,800-won lunchbox.

Being frugal and being squeezed are different.
{name} wanted to hold that line.

Still, the Broke Room memes crossed his mind sometimes, and he laughed alone.

title: The Truth About Pump Rooms
description:
He finally joined a stock pump room.

'300% returns guaranteed' 'Free pick revealed today only.'
The room had 500 people. Profit screenshots posted by the minute.

The 'Leader' called a stock. Buy recommendation.
The room cheered. 'We trust you, Leader!'

{name} hovered his finger over the buy button.

But suddenly — are all those profit proofs real.
If they're all true, why is the Leader charging membership fees.

choices.text: Buy the called stock. Everyone's winning, I can't be left out.
choices.result_text:
He bought the Leader's pick.

The first few days it rose. {name} posted a proof shot too. 'Thank you, Leader!'

Then one day, the stock crashed.
The Leader said 'cutting losses is strategy too' and called the next pick.
The room cheered again.

Only then did he see it. What the Leader earned wasn't the stocks — it was the fees.
And that nobody ever posts their losses.

choices.text: Leave the room. Nobody teaches strangers how to make free money.
choices.result_text:
{name} lifted his finger off the buy button.
And left the room.

Real experts make money quietly with their own cash.
They don't charge fees to call stocks for strangers.

More than 500 profit proofs, that one simple logic protected {name}.

Days later, that room made the news as a scam.
{name} didn't read the article to the end. He already knew.

title: Margin Call D-1
description:
2 AM. The HTS screen is red.

Stocks bought on margin loan are near the daily limit-down for the second day.
A notification popped up in the brokerage app.

'Insufficient collateral. Additional deposit or forced liquidation scheduled (D-1).'

Forced liquidation. The moment the market opens tomorrow, the brokerage will dump {name}'s stocks.
At market price. For a pittance.

{name} checked the account. There was no money for an additional deposit.
The greed bought on borrowed money was returning with the weight of what was borrowed.

choices.text: Scrape together money to hold it — selling here ends everything
choices.result_text:
Card loans, emergency cash, everything he could pull together.

He barely met the collateral. The liquidation was stopped.

But stopping it wasn't the end.
If the price keeps falling, he has to stop it again. And again. And again.

Only then did {name} understand.
Leverage isn't something you hold off — it's something you escape.
Late, but next time he'd remember.

choices.text: Accept the liquidation — cutting losses is skill too
choices.result_text:
{name} didn't make the deposit.

The next morning, the stocks were force-liquidated at market price.
The loss was big. His account staggered.

But strangely, his mind felt lighter.
He'd stopped pouring water into a bottomless jar.

The first lesson of leverage — what you bought with debt was never yours.
An expensive lesson, but he ended it in one stroke.

title: The Second Job at Night
description:
The salary alone doesn't add up.

{name} registered as a delivery app rider.
Day job by day, deliveries by night. Everyone lives like this these days, they said.

First call. One fried chicken, 1.2km, 3,200 won delivery fee.
He put on the helmet and headed into the night streets.

Raindrops began to fall.
The next call appeared on the phone mount screen.

choices.text: Ride even in the rain — there's a rain surcharge
choices.result_text:
Rainy days have more calls, and surcharges.
That much more dangerous, that much more earned.

{name} rode until 1 AM.
Wet clothes, frozen hands, 48,000 won logged in the account.

His body felt like it would break, but the numbers were honest.
Filling it this way is how the day-job salary stays whole.

Gangnam, somewhere in this rain, was getting one call closer.

choices.text: Call it a night — an accident in the rain costs more
choices.result_text:
{name} took off the helmet.

Slip on a wet road for 3,200 won, and the hospital bill is 300,000.
The math didn't add up.

Not pushing too hard was a strategy too.
For someone whose body is the asset, protecting the body was money itself.

{name} bought a warm convenience store coffee and walked home.
Today's earnings: 30,000 won. But not a scratch on him.
